# #4112: Patch: a pull request that changes only the mutation-testing settings or scripts no longer runs the CI jobs that never read them
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
The project has a weekly mutation-testing run, with its own settings file and scripts. The script that picks which checks a pull request needs gets them wrong: it takes the settings file for a build setting, and the scripts for something the website reads. So a pull request touching them runs almost every check: the engine's and the AI's test groups, the web's unit shards, the end-to-end smoke. None of those checks reads these files.

Such pull requests are common, because the ongoing mutation audit edits the settings file with every batch. Every needless check waits in the same queue as everyone else's work. Once this is built:
- a pull request that changes the shared crate and the settings file runs the checks the shared crate needs, as it would without the settings file;
- a pull request that changes only the mutation scripts runs none of the heavy checks. The mutation workflow still tests it on its own.

## Why
- `scripts/ci-scope.sh:291` reads `Cargo.toml | Cargo.lock | rust-toolchain.toml | .cargo/* | .github/* | scripts/ci-scope.sh)` and turns on `clippy $RUST web web_promote e2e`. `.cargo/*` is there for `.cargo/config.toml`, which cargo reads. `.cargo/mutants.toml` is cargo-mutants' own file, which no build reads; only `scripts/mutants.sh` and `.github/workflows/mutants.yml` name it.
- `scripts/mutants.sh`, `scripts/mutants-runner.sh` and `scripts/pool-probe.sh` fall through to `*) on web` and `*) on e2e`. The e2e case lists the scripts no build runs (`browse.sh`, the two promote scripts, `server-image.sh`, `worktree.sh`) and leaves these three out.
- No `ci.yml` job runs any of them: `grep mutants .github/workflows/ci.yml` finds nothing. The code that names them does so only in comments (`crates/engine/src/testkit/pool_probe.rs:7`, `crates/run/src/tests.rs:987`, the two Stryker configs).
- `mutants.yml`'s `pull_request.paths` already list `.cargo/mutants.toml`, `scripts/mutants.sh` and `scripts/mutants-runner.sh`, so a change to them keeps a check that does read them.
- Since 2026-10-01, `.cargo/mutants.toml` changed in 18 commits on `main`. In 13 of them, every other file sat under `crates/shared/` or `crates/run/`, or was `scripts/mutants.sh`. These are the #3513 and #3593 audit batches: 317174aa76, 11274b4844, e4f70ffd2f, c4fbb5d7ae, f65478fb79, e41b3d174c, eb59ecbd78, 562883049a, 63d7b1a286, 4ff211a4e3, a98affd22b, 48a8587363, bd47844434.
  - For a `crates/shared` change, the crate map runs `rust_server` and `rust_tools_wasm`.
  - The settings file added the three engine rules jobs, `engine`, `engine golden`, `cards lib`, `cards`, `ai`, `ai slow` and `web (promote-production)`, each compiling on its own.
  - bd47844434 changed only `mutants.toml` and `mutants.sh`, and ran every Rust group, every web job and all four e2e smoke shards.
  - #4038 (open) will edit `mutants.sh` again.
- CLAUDE.md, CI: every push runs on the organization's shared runners, and the runner gate lets only six CI and CD runs go at once, pull requests last.

## Proposal
- Add `.cargo/mutants.toml`, `scripts/mutants.sh`, `scripts/mutants-runner.sh` and `scripts/pool-probe.sh` to `ci-scope.sh`'s skip list (`skipped()`), as a new class in the header's description of the list: the mutation-testing tooling, which `mutants.yml` runs and checks on its own trigger, and the pool probe, which a person runs.
- Restate in the header the proof that nothing in `crates/`, `apps/`, `e2e/` or `spec/` reads these files, as CLAUDE.md asks of a path joining the list.
- The effect: a diff of only those files runs `bot selftest` alone in `ci.yml`, beside `mutants.yml`'s own run. Beside other files they are skipped, and the diff scopes as those files do.
- Leave the rest as it is: `.cargo/config.toml` and every other `.cargo/` file keep running every job. `.github/mutants-floor.txt` and `mutants.yml` keep running everything, as all of `.github/` does, and `ci-scope.test.ts` pins the floor file.
- Update the header's lines on what `.cargo/` and the scripts turn on.

Rejected alternative: a case that turns on no line but leaves `full` true. A diff of mutation tooling alone would still run the release builds, `rust (checks, fuzz 200)` and `rust (classify)`, none of which reads it.

## Where it lands
- `scripts/ci-scope.sh` (the skip list and its header)
- `apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] In `ci-scope.test.ts`, each of the four files alone, and each beside `bot/harness/state.py`, gives `full=false`. This fails on today's script.
- [ ] `crates/shared/src/lib.rs` beside `.cargo/mutants.toml` turns on exactly the lines `crates/shared/src/lib.rs` alone does. Likewise, `crates/run/src/lib.rs` beside `scripts/mutants.sh` turns on exactly what `crates/run/src/lib.rs` alone does. Both fail today.
- [ ] `.cargo/config.toml` still runs every job but the db suites (the existing cargo-settings test passes unchanged), and `.github/mutants-floor.txt` still runs everything.
- [ ] The tests that hold the script to the paths the web's and e2e's sources name still pass.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/net/ci-scope.test.ts` passes.
- [ ] The header names the four paths and why each is on the list.

## Size and risks
- **Size:** small, **difficulty:medium**: about 10 lines of script and 20 of test.
- **Timing:** it takes effect on the pull requests after it lands, since `ci.yml`'s `changes` job runs `main`'s copy of the script (#2986). The pull request that makes it runs everything.
- **Risk:** a later CI job that starts reading one of these files must take it off the list in the same pull request; the header says so. A push to `main` and the daily super run still run everything, whatever changed.
